A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same MedVLSynther study. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A–I.

before.justification: Tables 2–6 report original medical VQA experiments, including pipeline, dataset-size, generator/verifier and training-method ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original human-audit results, dataset analyses and detailed contamination findings in the appendices.

M1.justification: The generator–verifier pipeline, essential gates, normalized scoring rule, acceptance threshold and SFT/RLVR procedures remain unchanged. Appendix E discloses full prompts. The expanded archetype list in Section 3.2 matches categories already shown in v1 Figure 2 and does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MedSynVQA corpus and six medical VQA benchmarks, retaining the reported modality and anatomy coverage. The new human audits, statistics and examples examine existing data rather than extending its task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands the PMC-style comparison into separate text-only and text–image generation controls. The original control's scores are retained under the text–image label, alongside an additional text-only row for each student size. Table 6's comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The main benchmark protocol, student sizes and default 5K training setting remain unchanged. v2 adds a supplementary human-review protocol involving five specialists, 15 accepted and 20 rejected items, four rating criteria, and differentiated author/clinician review. Table 2 also separates generation conditions with and without images.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary validation through human quality and rejection audits, rubric pass-rate and student-answer distributions, and detailed generated-item and model-output case studies. Appendix F supplies detailed evidence for the contamination analysis that v1 only briefly asserted. Existing main-text ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The existing uncertainty presentation is retained, without newly specified seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added rating means, similarity summaries and correct-answer distributions describe outcomes rather than introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 3–6 retain their results. Table 2 newly reports text-only averages of 54.25/54.41, while the original 54.80/55.15 values appear as text–image results. Substantial supplementary findings include acceptance of 14/15 audited accepted items, disagreement with three of four vocabulary-based rejections, and 47 flagged semantic text pairs across 23 test queries; these flags are not established duplicates.

T1.justification: The sample definition and normalized quality-score equation remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced; the appendix audit metrics provide procedural documentation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about rubric-guided synthesis, open reproducibility, benchmark improvements and contamination avoidance. Additional supporting material does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly identifies context-misreading false rejections, inadequate wording checks, image-usability problems and the small human-study limitation. Appendices C and I add research-only applicability and reasoning qualifications. Some explanations conflict: Appendix H endorses rejecting caption-supported demographics despite the source-aware policy and Appendix G's criticism of such rejections.

D1.justification: v2 supplies full generation/verifier prompts and JSON contracts, A100 hardware and mixed-precision information, licensing/provenance handling, a stated data/code/model release location, and detailed contamination-audit implementation. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to the underlying training procedure.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged. Appendix F uses already-listed embedding and retrieval references to explain audit implementation, without substantively revising research positioning.

P1.justification: The existing main narrative and section sequence remain largely verbatim. Limited edits update archetype terminology and the publication header, add acknowledgments and disclosures, and organize supplementary material into Appendices A–I.

P2.justification: v2 expands and relabels Table 2, adds Tables 7–11 and Figures 5–6, and introduces extensive prompt boxes and illustrated case panels. Existing tables reflow and Figure 4 moves, while Figures 1–4 otherwise retain their content.

improvement.justification: Full prompts, audit procedures and the small human study improve reproducibility and scrutiny of claims previously supported only indirectly. However, Section 4.2 retains outdated text-only score descriptions, Appendix F's blanket no-image-overlap statement conflicts with Figure 6's same-source variant, and Appendix I includes mismatched commentary, such as discussing the page-36 thoracic CT case as brain MRI. These reporting problems limit the net quality gain.
